question: Leonardo spent years preparing a giant bronze horse for Milan's ruler. What became of the bronze set aside for it?
answer: It went into cannon. In 1494, with a French army marching into Italy, Ludovico Sforza sent the metal to his father-in-law in Ferrara to be cast into guns. Leonardo's full-size clay model stood for five more years, until French soldiers took Milan in 1499 and used it for target practice. The horse was never cast.
move: A project that takes years competes with every emergency in between.
ask: Which slow, important project of mine keeps losing its time to whatever feels urgent this week?
trap: French troops, because they did ruin the clay model later.
reference: Walter Isaacson, Leonardo da Vinci, Simon & Schuster, 2017
